key_insight: This study compares three ways to evaluate enterprise analytics agents: judging execution traces, judging text with red-teaming, and applying deterministic rules. The supplied abstract is incomplete, so it does not establish which approach performs best.
problem_solved: How to reliably detect failures in LLM-based analytics agents that carry out complex workflows across multiple tools.
method: Conduct a three-phase comparison of three evaluation paradigms: trace-based LLM judging, text-only LLM judging with red-teaming, and deterministic heuristics.
Apply each framework to two analytics agents in a controlled research setting.
Use frozen execution traces to compare evaluations on fixed agent behavior rather than changing runs.
impact: The comparison can help practitioners reason about evaluation choices for enterprise agents. Specific performance advantages and recommendations cannot be confirmed from the provided excerpt.
visual_elements: Three-column comparison of evaluation paradigms, showing the evidence each uses.
Workflow diagram showing two analytics agents producing frozen traces for evaluation.
Multi-tool execution timeline with potential failure points highlighted.
Evaluation-goals panel highlighting stability, failure detection, and discovery, without unsupported scores.
paper_title: Comparative Analysis of Agent Evaluation Frameworks: Stability, Detection, and Discovery in Enterprise Analytics Agents
paper_authors: Howard Zhang, Chuck Arvin, Logan Brown, Mihir Bhatia, Neelu Choudhary
